items.title: Perez gets a five-place Qatar drop after the Vegas clash
items.summary: Stewards' Document 61 found Perez wholly responsible for the Turn 14 collision with Rafael Câmara and converted his unserved 10-second penalty into five places at his next race. In a later Formula1.com report, Perez said he thought he was alongside; Câmara said he still needed to review what happened.
items.why_it_matters: Apply the five places in Qatar grid preparation. Keep the drivers' accounts separate from the stewards' finding and do not copy Vegas power-unit penalties or energy limits into Qatar event data.

sources.label: Formula1.com report and driver reactions, full article checked

items.title: Qatar's 27-lap cap; official F1 reports conflict on set totals
items.summary: Two Formula1.com articles published on 25 November give different per-driver allocations: the 10:05 UTC guide says 2 C1 Hard, 3 C2 Medium and 8 C3 Soft, with an extra Soft reserved for Q3; the 10:43 UTC explainer says each driver gets 13 sets (2 C1, 4 C2, 7 C3). Pirelli's 24 November release confirms the compounds and 27-lap cap, but not set totals. The FIA competition visa confirms 57 race laps over 5.419 km and a 19:00 local start. Its separate Pirelli competition notes prescribe C1 and C2 as mandatory race tyres, C3 for Q3, and 27 laps per set across tyre history; they do not state the conflicting per-driver allocation. Pirelli's reported counting rules include Safety Car and Virtual Safety Car laps; all race laps from start signal to chequered flag count, an unfinished lap in other sessions counts in full, mixed-mileage sets take the higher count, and reconnaissance, formation and post-race laps are excluded.
items.why_it_matters: Do not present a single per-driver inventory as settled: cite the competing official reports until clarified. The 27-lap cap and FIA/Pirelli prescription are separately reviewed, but exact remaining-set counts still require a post-qualifying official chart.

items.title: FIA lists Audi's Tsunoda appeal; decision not yet published
items.summary: The FIA scheduled a closed International Court of Appeal hearing in Paris for 09:00 local time on 25 November on Audi's appeal of Italian GP Document 69, where stewards took no further action after the extra formation lap. The public notice says a decision will be published after the hearing; as checked at 19:38 UTC, no later FIA decision was found. Las Vegas Document 66's championship-points paper also notes Audi's appeal. Formula1.com currently lists Antonelli 402 / Verstappen 304 and Mercedes 666 / Ferrari 517 after round 21.
items.why_it_matters: The hearing notice does not impose a penalty or change the points table. Do not infer a result; refresh standings and re-evaluate the appeal only if the Court publishes a decision.

items.title: Haas confirms Câmara for Qatar; Slater takes his F2 seat
items.summary: Haas confirmed on 22 November that Câmara will drive for the team at both remaining 2026 Grands Prix, ahead of his 2027 F1 campaign. Formula1.com reported on 24 November that Freddie Slater will take over Câmara's Invicta F2 seat for the final two rounds; the article says Câmara had led the F2 standings.
items.why_it_matters: Câmara's Qatar F1 participation is settled, but the F2 driver change does not alter the Haas F1 line-up or establish any FP1 substitutions.
